A.explanation: This has $\text{s}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{s}^{-3}$ because the watt was not fully expanded to $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-3}$.

B.explanation: This has $\text{s}^{-2}$ which is the unit of force times distance divided by time incorrectly, not power which is energy per unit time.

C.explanation: After cancelling $\text{m}^2$ with $\text{m}^{-2}$ and $\text{K}^4$ with $\text{K}^{-4}$, $L$ has the unit of power, $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-3}$.

D.explanation: This has an extra $\text{s}^{-1}$ factor, as if $T^4$ contributed an extra $\text{s}^{-1}$ instead of cancelling the $\text{K}^{-4}$ in $\sigma$.

hints: Notice the equation $L = 4\pi r^2 \sigma T^4$ with $r$ in $\text{m}$, $T$ in $\text{K}$ and $\sigma$ in $\text{W m}^{-2}\text{K}^{-4}$ - the numbers $4\pi$ have no units.
Connect the watt to SI base units using $1 \text{ W} = 1 \text{ J s}^{-1}$ and $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$ with $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Combine $r^2$ in $\text{m}^2$ and $T^4$ in $\text{K}^4$ with $\sigma$ and cancel $\text{m}^{-2}$ with $\text{m}^2$ and $\text{K}^{-4}$ with $\text{K}^4$ to leave the base units of power.
walkthrough: Identify the units to combine: $[r^2] = \text{m}^2$, $[T^4] = \text{K}^4$, and $[\sigma] = \text{W m}^{-2}\text{K}^{-4}$, while $4\pi$ is dimensionless.
Express the watt in SI base units: $1 \text{ W} = 1 \text{ J s}^{-1}$, $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$, and $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$, so $1 \text{ W} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2\text{s}^{-3}$.
Substitute into the equation for units: $[L] = \text{m}^2 \times (\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-3} \text{ m}^{-2}\text{K}^{-4}) \times \text{K}^4$.
This is the SI base-unit form of power, which matches the luminosity as energy radiated per unit time. This is option C.
